official_measurement_examples.name: NNR current national geometry
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England's national NNR dataset was last updated 29 April 2026 and excludes proposed sites, so proposed or historic reserve proposals must not be treated as current declared NNR geometry.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning Data current count
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Data reported 224 National Nature Reserves with its collector last run 23 July 2026 and new data found 22 July 2026; this is a current aggregation layer, not a substitute for declaration documents.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 declaration changes
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England published 2026 notices for new, extended or renamed NNRs including Cheltenham Escarpment, Mid Cornwall Moors and Seven Sisters, showing reserve geometry and naming can change over time.

official_measurement_examples.name: LNR authoritative-source limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England's July 2026 national LNR dataset explicitly says it is indicative rather than definitive and that local authorities provide definitive current information.

official_measurement_examples.name: LNR declaration control
official_measurement_examples.fact: Local authority guidance requires control of LNR land through ownership, lease or agreement and a declaration boundary aligned with or within the authority's legal land control.

official_measurement_examples.name: Public access limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Nature reserve status does not create unrestricted public access; access can be restricted where needed to protect wildlife and existing statutory access rights remain separate.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: NNR or LNR designation is a conservation status and management framework, not planning permission or a parcel development-capacity decision.

official_measurement_examples.name: Protected-site overlap
official_measurement_examples.fact: Nature reserve boundaries may overlap SSSI, Habitats Regulations or other designations, and each applicable legal or planning control must be assessed separately.

core_rules: a National Nature Reserve dataset record is not planning permission
a proposed reserve is not a declared National Nature Reserve
current NNR geometry must retain declaration and revision date context
a Local Nature Reserve national dataset is indicative and not definitive local-authority evidence
absence from the national LNR aggregation is not proof no valid local declaration exists
LNR declaration requires legal land control but does not prove private ownership of every underlying interest
reserve public access is not necessarily unrestricted access
reserve designation does not itself determine dwelling yield or development capacity
NNR or LNR status does not replace SSSI Habitats Regulations species or other applicable controls
a recent declaration extension or renaming must not be merged with historic geometry without date handling
reserve management responsibility is not land-development authority
nature-reserve evidence does not create access rights for a development parcel
declaration maps must not be inferred from approximate proximity
reserve status does not reserve utilities transport or infrastructure capacity
no parcel nature-reserve clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official Natural England, GOV.UK, data.gov.uk and Planning Data sources checked on 2026-07-26. April-July 2026 NNR/LNR data and 2026 declaration notices were kept distinct from proposed sites, definitive local records and planning permission.
